items.title: UKPNP Denounces Denial of Entry to Pakistani Opposition Leaders Visiting Azad Kashmir Protests
items.author: By The Mirror Jammu Kashmir Special Correspondent
items.excerpt: Exiled rights party condemns federal blockage of National Assembly and Senate delegation to Rawalakot sit-in, warning of severe food and medical shortages under an ongoing security blockade.

heroImage.caption: UKPNP Denounces Denial of Entry to Pakistani Opposition Leaders Visiting Azad Kashmir Protests — High-level parliamentary delegation blocked at entry checkpoints — The Mirror Jammu Kashmir

body.text: GENEVA / ISLAMABAD — The United Kashmir People's National Party (UKPNP) has issued a stinging condemnation of Pakistani authorities following the blockage of a high-level parliamentary delegation attempting to visit protest sites in Azad Kashmir.

Federal security forces turned back members of the National Assembly and Senate at key entry checkpoints leading into Rawalakot, where local civil society and activist groups have been conducting prolonged sit-in demonstrations against regional administrative policies and resource allocation.
Blocking elected representatives from observing the situation on the ground only deepens the sense of isolation and severe governance deficit across the region.
Local leadership has reported acute shortages of basic medical supplies and essential food items as security blockades surrounding the district remain enforced for the third consecutive week.

items.title: UKPNP Demands End to Unrest and Lethal Crackdown in Azad Kashmir
items.author: Special Correspondent
items.excerpt: UKPNP unreservedly condemns escalating force and extrajudicial killings in Kotli and Rawalakot, calling for an immediate halt to security operations, lifting of media blackouts, and an independent judicial inquiry.

heroImage.caption: UKPNP Demands End to Unrest and Lethal Crackdown in Azad Kashmir — Protests expand across Kotli and Rawalakot amid total communications blackout — The Mirror Jammu Kashmir

body.text: GENEVA / RAWALAKOT — Expanding civil unrest across Kotli and Rawalakot has prompted urgent calls for restraint after reports emerged of lethal force being used against civilian demonstrations.

The United Kashmir People's National Party called for an immediate suspension of security operations and advocated for the restoration of internet and mobile telecommunication feeds that have remained disrupted across major urban centers.

Human rights defenders have emphasized that a high-level, independent judicial commission must be established to investigate extrajudicial casualties and compensate affected civilian families without delay.

items.title: UKPNP AND SKHRC STAGE PROTEST OUTSIDE UN GENEVA OVER AZAD KASHMIR CRACKDOWN DURING UNHRC 62ND SESSION IN GENEVA
items.author: The Mirror Jammu Kashmir Special Correspondent
items.excerpt: Representatives of UKPNP and SKHRC staged a high-profile demonstration outside UN Geneva, submitting an urgent memorandum demanding an independent OHCHR fact-finding mission.

heroImage.caption: UKPNP and SKHRC members protesting outside the UN headquarters in Geneva during the UNHRC session.

body.text: GENEVA — Parallel to the ongoing 62nd Session of the United Nations Human Rights Council, human rights advocates and Kashmiri diaspora members gathered at the Place des Nations outside the UN headquarters.

Holding banners highlighting fundamental rights violations, delegates formally submitted a memorandum addressed to the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights calling for a dedicated fact-finding delegation to inspect ground realities in Azad Kashmir.

items.title: Escalating Violent Crackdown in Azad Kashmir Triggers Global Calls for Media Access and Independent Inquiry
items.author: Editorial Desk
items.excerpt: UKPNP condemns lethal firing on protesters in Rawalakot following the killing of activist Shahzaib Habib; demands UN intervention and immediate lifting of media blackout.

heroImage.caption: Escalating Violent Crackdown in Azad Kashmir — Deadly firing outside Rawalakot CMH sparks international outcry and demands for media access — The Mirror Jammu Kashmir

body.text: RAWALAKOT — Global human rights monitors have voiced deep alarm following incidents of direct firing outside the Combined Military Hospital (CMH) in Rawalakot, following the death of local activist Shahzaib Habib.

International press freedom organizations have urged federal authorities to grant immediate, unhindered access to independent journalists and international media crews to ensure factual reporting from the region.

items.title: HUMAN RIGHTS ALERT: Urgent UN Intervention Demanded as Civilians Killed in Rawalakot Crackdown
items.author: Human Rights Desk
items.excerpt: UKPNP expresses grave concern after Frontier Corps forces open direct fire on peaceful sit-in protesters at Eid Gah Ground in Rawalakot, leaving two civilians dead and several critically injured.

heroImage.caption: Human Rights Alert: Operations at Eid Gah Ground in Rawalakot trigger global calls for UN intervention — The Mirror Jammu Kashmir

body.text: RAWALAKOT — An urgent human rights dispatch has been circulated to international mechanisms after security forces intervened at the Eid Gah Ground sit-in demonstration in Rawalakot.
Reports confirm two civilian casualties and multiple injuries following the escalation, sparking renewed appeals for immediate diplomatic and humanitarian oversight.

items.title: UKPNP Condemns Fatal Attack on Activist Vehicle, Calls for Independent Probe in Azad Kashmir
items.author: Editorial Desk
items.excerpt: United Kashmir People's National Party strongly condemns the violent attack in Poonch district that killed Shahzaib Habib and injured JAAC leader Umar Nazir, demanding an independent inquiry and reversal of the ban on JAAC.

heroImage.caption: Strong Condemnation of the Martyrdom of Shahzeb Habib & Attack on Umar Nazir Kashmiri — The Mirror Jammu Kashmir

body.text: POONCH / RAWALAKOT — Political representatives and community organizations have united in condemning a targeted attack on an activist vehicle traveling through Poonch district.

The incident resulted in the fatal shooting of Shahzaib Habib and critical injuries to Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) activist Umar Nazir. Civil society bodies have reiterated demands for an impartial inquiry into the circumstances surrounding the violence.
